title: add-prompt-order-robustness-assertion-ci-check
author: Sofia Tran
commits: a1f34b: initial prompt-order robustness checker and sampling harness
b2c88d: add CI workflow & small unit tests
c9d0e1: reduce wall-clock by adaptive-sample-size + caching
d4f9a2: docs for permutation stability metric and failure guidance
e5ab3f: tighten seeding/fixture to remove flakiness
description:
Why: We see subtle regressions where model outputs are sensitive to the ordering of prompts in a prompt set (e.g., system + instruction + few-shot examples). This PR introduces an automated CI assertion that measures ordering robustness by permuting prompt components/samples and computing a stability score. The goal is to catch regressions where small reorderings cause material differences in model ranking/quality for a prompt-set used in downstream checks.

What:
- New metric: Permutation Stability Score (PSS) — median pairwise Kendall Tau over N random permutations (normalized to [0,1]). Lower values indicate order-sensitive outputs.
- CI check: ci/checks/prompt-order-robustness.yml runs a sampled stability job for changed prompt-sets and fails if PSS < 0.85 or disagreement_rate > 0.05.
- Lightweight sampling harness with adaptive sample size: starts with 10 permutations and increases up to 60 only when variance is high to bound runtime.
- Deterministic reseeding and memoized model-call cache during CI to reduce flakiness and wall time.
- Unit tests for the metric, plus an integration smoke test that validates behavior against a mocked model.
- Docs: guidance for engineers on interpreting PSS failures and recommended mitigations (reformatting prompts, anchor examples, or targeted evals).

Risk/Scope: This adds a new CI check in eval pipelines only (does not affect serving). The default thresholds are conservative so we minimize false positives. The adaptive sampling and caching are tuned to keep CI latency under the existing eval budget.

How to review: Focus on correctness of the PSS implementation (perm_stability_metric.py), determinism under seeding fixtures (tests), and the CI workflow memory/timeout parameters. The implementation is intentionally modular so teams can enable the check per-prompt-set via metadata in defaults.yaml.

Related: ENG-3219 tracks rollout / opt-in across monorepo eval suites. PM-78 is the product ticket for adding prompt-robustness signals to the quality dashboard.

Backstory: This PR emerged from an incident where a canary failed sporadically when a front-end change re-ordered example blocks; a follow-up audit showed sensitive ranking deltas tied to order. We need a smoke/assertion to prevent regressions that are invisible to token-level metrics.

Notes: The description and docs include examples illustrating a failing prompt-set and suggested fixes. The CI job will run only for changed prompt-set directories (opt-in by adding metadata in defaults.yaml).
review_thread:
Priya Nair: Please add a short description of PSS to the docs and justify the 0.85 threshold.
Sofia Tran: Added docs + rationale; threshold chosen from historical eval of stable prompt-sets (median ~0.92) but set conservatively at 0.85 to allow some noise.
Liam Brooks: Initially flagged flaky test in test_prompt_order_stability — failed intermittently on CI.
Sofia Tran: Investigated; root cause was nondeterministic fixture seeding and redundant network calls. Added deterministic seed propagation and memoized model call cache — reran CI.
Anika Desai: Asked for adaptive sampling to avoid 60-permutation worst case on every run.
Sofia Tran: Implemented adaptive sample size, added comments explaining tradeoffs, and added a small benchmark in tests to show median runtime at ~45s on build agents.
Priya Nair: Approved after minor doc edits.
Liam Brooks: Approved and left a note that threshold/alpha should be configurable per-team.
Merge: squash and merge after green CI.
release_notes:
- Added Permutation Stability Score (PSS) and CI assertion to detect prompt-order sensitivity.
- New eval harness hook: prompt_order_stability_checker.py.
- CI workflow: prompt-order-robustness.yml (opt-in per prompt-set).
- Documentation: docs/eval/permutation_stability.md with troubleshooting and mitigations.
